title: Cholera: Protect Your Family
subtitle: A one-page guide for households

summary.topic: What cholera is, how it spreads, how to prevent it at home, and when to get help.
key_points: Cholera spreads through food or water contaminated with the bacterium *Vibrio cholerae*.
Safe water, handwashing with soap and safe food handling prevent it.
Severe watery diarrhoea can kill within hours: get treatment quickly.
summary.takeaway: Clean water, soap and quick treatment save lives.

disclaimer: General information only, not medical advice. Talk to a qualified health worker about your own situation.

blocks.text: Cholera is an acute diarrhoeal infection caused by consuming food or water contaminated with the bacterium *Vibrio cholerae*. Most people infected have no symptoms or mild ones, but they can still spread the bacteria in their faeces for 1 to 10 days. Symptoms appear 12 hours to 5 days after infection (WHO, 2026).

items: **Wash hands** with soap and clean water, especially before handling food and after using the toilet.
**Drink safe water:** boiled, bottled or purified.
**Store food and water safely**, covered and clean.
**Use a toilet or latrine** and dispose of faeces safely.

blocks.text: The oral cholera vaccine (OCV) can also help prevent and control cholera. Ask your clinic whether it is offered in your area.

blocks.title: Go to a clinic quickly
blocks.text: Severe watery diarrhoea can be fatal within hours if not treated. Most people can be treated with **oral rehydration solution (ORS)**; severe cases need intravenous fluids, ORS and antibiotics from health workers.
